source.declared_content: 4 inputs, 1 output, 3 D-type flip-flops, 2 inverters, 8 gates (1 AND, 1 NAND, 2 OR, 4 NOR)
source.note: The netlist self-declares its gate counts but its upstream source is not yet pinned. Record the repository and commit before publishing this result.

purpose: Sequential-state capture: proves the analyzer records flip-flop state across samples, which a purely combinational benchmark cannot show.

verification.reproducibility: Two independent physical captures returned the same trigger word 0x4018.

notes: The 46408-byte configuration size is fixed and is not a utilization metric.
Capture time is one Windows host measurement including Python startup and serial transport.
The baseline has unused SPI input pins optimized away; compare logic resources, not I/O timing.
Analyzer-only cost cross-checks at 116 LUTs against logic4 (116) and is the expected constant for the capture core.
s27 is a very small sequential circuit, so the percentage frequency overhead is dominated by the analyzer, not by the benchmark.
This experiment validates instrumentation overhead and observed sequential behaviour, not ATPG or manufacturing fault coverage.
